Q1.title: Announcements versus required calendar milestones
Q1.question: Should #8 require an event, and should the existing MODEL label for #19 remain or be reopened as KEY/AMBIGUOUS?
Q1.recommendation: Keep #8 AMBIGUOUS and reopen #19 as AMBIGUOUS unless you can identify a supplied rule requiring these milestones. Record any new mandatory-milestone policy as a future rule.
Q1.alternatives: Operational dates belong on the executive calendar; or the no-action/FYI instruction permits leaving announcements without attendance or hold requests unbooked.

Q2.title: Explicit delegation to choose a slot
Q2.question: Approve changing #14 from saved KEY to MODEL?
Q2.recommendation: Yes. The explicit instruction to pick one grants scheduling discretion; creating only a decision reminder does not fulfill it.
Q2.alternatives: Treat pick one as delegated choice; or require the principal to choose despite no such restriction in the supplied instructions.

Q3.title: Requests delivered after their deadlines
Q3.question: For these stale requests, how should model credit be treated: backfill required, no action acceptable, or unresolved/excluded from capability attribution?
Q3.recommendation: Retain the settled KEY and PLAN defects and leave model credit unresolved. Do not invent a backfill requirement or treat arbitrary new dates as authorized.
Q3.alternatives: Historical calendar/task recording remains mechanically possible; prospective fulfillment is already impossible and instructions supply no recovery policy.

Q4.title: Undated reminders and qualitative event times
Q4.question: Which reminder timing should receive credit without a stated deadline, and how should launch night constrain an unspecified event hour?
Q4.recommendation: Preserve definite KEY findings while withholding model credit unless the email establishes an admissible window. Keep the uncounted livestream-hour disagreement separate from the definite duration issue.
Q4.alternatives: A pragmatic reminder may be useful without satisfying an unstated deadline. Night may override a morning default, but the source does not uniquely select 20:00.

Q5.title: Conflicting timing within available emails
Q5.question: Which date controls athlete preparation (#26/#27), and does the one-pager (#28) need to precede the final or only the board presentation? Two uncounted sibling questions also need interpretation: does delaying launch move the ad-review deadline, and which rehearsal date controls?
Q5.recommendation: Keep the definite KEY findings. Leave model credit unresolved unless an evidence-based reading resolves the conflict; #28 has reviewer disagreement. Preserve the ancillary sibling questions without adding them to the 75-check coverage totals.
Q5.alternatives: The athlete’s explicit August 22 date versus the newer next-week wording; the one-pager’s before-final subject versus its ahead-of-board body. Neither supports the key’s exact deadlines.

Q6.title: Confirmations that repair a missing appointment
Q6.question: May the #33 confirmation create the still-future August 25 intro when no matching appointment exists?
Q6.recommendation: Leave attribution AMBIGUOUS unless the supplied confirmation guidance is interpreted to settle repair of missing state. The creation is not a duplicate or a revival of the cancelled retail-sponsor call.
Q6.alternatives: Confirmation-only no-op under explicit guidance; or reconcile the absent, previously requested appointment. Neither authorizes the invented 14:00 start.

Q7.title: Conditional requests and ownership of work
Q7.question: Does #38 require brainstorming despite conditional wording, and may #44 track Marketing’s deadline as a CEO oversight task?
Q7.recommendation: Keep both AMBIGUOUS. Use the supplied personal-assistant instructions; do not infer a universal ownership or brainstorming rule from receipt alone.
Q7.alternatives: A deadline may justify a coordination reminder; conditional wording or an explicitly different owner may instead make the message informational for the CEO.

Q8.title: Failed tool connection and model-quality attribution
Q8.question: Should the affected saved checks be reported separately or excluded from model-capability attribution while retaining their factual state results?
Q8.recommendation: Report them separately as infrastructure-limited. Preserve independently established KEY/PLAN/GRADER facts, and withhold model-performance conclusions. This audit does not alter scores or authorize any rerun.
Q8.alternatives: Judge the resulting store regardless of tool availability; or distinguish that outcome from model reasoning. Six audited capture days show failed secretary MCP, absent tools, no calls and unchanged stores; 16 emails/17 targets lack observed reads.

Q9.title: Trip start window and calendar representation
Q9.question: Does from the week of August 3 fix departure to Monday, and what counts as representing the trip start?
Q9.recommendation: Keep #41/#43 unresolved. The literal wording and earlier mail do not uniquely establish Monday; require neither invented separate boundary markers nor an arbitrary Tuesday start. #42’s missing explicit August 9 endpoint is independently established.
Q9.alternatives: Treat the phrase as a Monday-through-Sunday trip, making the Dynamics visit one day late; or allow a start within that week, making August 4/6 first/third-day visits plausible. A coherent trip interval is another valid representation.

Q10.title: Calendar changes awaiting approval
Q10.question: Should the reveal and rehearsal be moved before the sender receives Mark’s okay?
Q10.recommendation: Keep #55/#56 unresolved. Preserve the certain stale-delivery and false duplicate-diagnostic findings separately; do not treat an unapproved proposal or invalid diagnostic as proof of a correct model decision.
Q10.alternatives: Treat the proposal as authority to tentatively update the calendar; or keep existing bookings until approval. Neither interpretation supplies a future correction to the already-past July dates.
